key_impacts: PHIVOLCS issued tsunami alert level 3 calling immediate evacuation for multiple coastal provinces.
Evacuations occurred; surveyed barangays reported about 80% of residents moved to safe places after the alert.
In parts of Guiuan, the warning arrived after the expected tsunami arrival time.
Communication problems (power cuts, phone issues, incorrect radio broadcast) delayed or distorted messages to communities.
No significant tsunami wave occurred and no damages were observed.
evidence_snippets: On 31 August 2012 a strong earthquake occurred in the Philippine Trench east of Eastern Samar.
At 09:01 pm PHIVOLCS issued alert level 3… including coastal areas of Northern Samar, Eastern Samar, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur.
However, no significant wave appeared and no damages were observed.
missing_information: Exact number of evacuees per locality is not provided.
Measured wave heights and site-specific arrival times are not detailed.
Damage and casualty figures are not quantified (none reported).

key_impacts: A tsunami alert was raised in late February 2010 following the distant Chile earthquake.
Because the source was distant, timing was less critical in the related survey.
The Chile event produced only a very small wave and no damages (as referenced in the comparison).
evidence_snippets: A tsunami alert was raised in the end of February 2010; the source… was distant (Chile).
Like the Chile earthquake of 27 February 2010… caused only a very small wave and no damages.
missing_information: Specific Philippine provinces or sites covered by the 2010 alert are not listed.
Numbers of evacuees and any measured wave heights are not provided.
